dedupe_keys.name: der cam distributed energy resources customer adoption model berkeley lab

description: DER-CAM, the Distributed Energy Resources Customer Adoption Model, is a decision support tool developed by researchers at Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory since 2000 to find optimal distributed energy resource investments for buildings and multi-energy microgrids. It formulates the design problem as a mixed-integer linear program, using linearised AC and DC optimal power flow and piecewise approximations of non-linear efficiency curves, and returns the optimal portfolio, sizing, placement and dispatch of generation, combined heat and power, storage and cooling while co-optimising stacked value streams such as load shifting, peak shaving, export agreements and ancillary services. Inputs are hourly load profiles, tariffs, technology costs and site topology; the objective is usually total annual energy cost, and resilience targets can be enforced. Coverage is any site, with no fixed geography. Access: the page states DER-CAM is publicly available and free to use through a registered desktop application, with a data-processing template and tutorial; no licence text is shown. Caveats: linearised physics, typical-year hourly inputs, and site data must be supplied. It suits microgrid design, investment appraisal and resilience planning and compares with HOMER and MicroGridsPy catalogued here.
